title: Unions urge court to force ruling in ‘loyalty question’ lawsuit
summary: Three months after a hearing on whether to block federal agencies from asking four politicized essay questions of every federal job applicant, a federal judge still has not issued a decision.

title: Interior’s use of park fee revenue raises questions over federal funding rules
summary: Lawmakers are seeking details on whether National Park Service visitor fees and pass revenue are being redirected under existing authorities, highlighting how discretionary funds are allocated across competing maintenance and capital priorities.

title: NSF is using its HQ move to revoke telework for workers with disabilities, employees say
summary: Most of the science agency’s workforce is currently teleworking, as they are being relocated to a new office building that is close to the former headquarters.

title: HHS plans AI pilot for employees who need more than chatbots
summary: The department hopes to learn how employees use more sophisticated AI capabilities and what it would take to deploy them across the agency.

title: AI skills are becoming part of the hiring baseline at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency
summary: The intelligence agency is reshaping training for both new and existing employees as it builds AI and data management into core job expectations across the workforce.

title: In rare move, full appeals court agrees to hear case challenging Trump’s ‘Article II’ firings
summary: Federal circuit courts typically hear cases via randomized three-judge panels, reserving review by the entire judicial bench for its most important cases.

title: Intelligence director hearing cancelled as Trump pushes for controversial voter bill
summary: The development guarantees that Bill Pulte — whose selection to temporarily lead the office derailed a recent FISA vote — would start as acting national intelligence director on Friday.

title: FEMA, OMB noms grilled on alleged political sway in government assistance
summary: Democratic senators pointed to disparities between what states are approved to receive disaster funding as well as a proposal to require that political appointees approve grant awards to ensure they advance the president’s priorities.

title: AI is taking parts of background checks from 'months to hours,' clearance agency says
summary: A Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency official says advanced AI can cut parts of the vetting process from months to hours.

title: Education's latest handoff tests the limits of its downsizing strategy
summary: The department says services and protections won't change as HHS and DOJ take on larger roles. Critics aren't convinced.

title: GOP’s VA overhaul bill narrows some employees’ rights, spurs privatization, union says
summary: The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act also would cut some vets’ disability benefits and push the Veterans Affairs Department to bring back telework in some form.

title: Federal agencies are getting more attention on social media — and more criticism
summary: Federal accounts are generating far more engagement on X than they did in the final year of the Biden administration, according to new research.

title: Sen. Warner probes whether cyber agency workforce cuts weakened state support
summary: The request comes as officials question whether workforce reductions have affected the federal government's ability to support local cybersecurity efforts.

title: Congress wants answers on Pentagon’s use of military lawyers in civilian jobs
summary: A bipartisan NDAA provision would require GAO to examine whether assigning JAGs to Justice Department work is affecting military readiness and morale.

title: The federal government has a major blind spot in how it evaluates programs
summary: COMMENTARY | Decades of design flaws have left agencies struggling to measure the impact of their major initiatives. It is time to move beyond compliance and build real, durable capacity.

title: NTEU sues IRS over destruction of employees’ pro-union decorations
summary: The Internal Revenue Service last month issued a directive barring employees from posting flyers and other decorations related to the National Treasury Employees Union, which the union says violates the First Amendment.

title: Who watches the watchdogs? GAO finds flaws in inspector general oversight system
summary: President Donald Trump has fired nearly 20 IGs, and his administration last year put a hold on funding for the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency.

title: White House cyber office hire triggers leadership changes inside infrastructure security agency
summary: A senior CISA official’s move sets off a series of internal assignments as the agency prepares to expand hiring after a year of workforce reductions and restructuring.

title: Can a championship run teach us something about government?
summary: COMMENTARY | We spend a lot of time looking for shortcuts, but the most meaningful progress in federal service — like in sports — requires something more durable than a quick win.

title: Anti-fraud overhaul clears House despite Democratic concerns over privacy and IG independence
summary: Many Democrats opposed the measure due to fears the Trump administration would exert more political influence on inspectors general as well as concerns about privacy risk.

title: Senate rejects Cyber Force push as debate over cyber structure continues
summary: Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand’s amendment to place a new service under the Army fell short in committee, even as lawmakers advanced separate provisions examining Cyber Command’s role and resourcing.

title: Lawmakers press for tighter oversight of fast-growing prediction markets
summary: Senators are urging the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to clarify rules for event contracts and strengthen monitoring standards, warning that rapid growth in prediction markets is exposing weaknesses in safeguards against manipulation and consumer harm.

title: Surveillance authority nears historic lapse as House deadlock meets intelligence leadership fight
summary: Section 702 is set to expire for the first time after a failed House vote, even as a White House nomination aims to resolve a separate battle over who should oversee the intelligence community during the transition.
